title: Positive-dimensional locally algebraic closed subsets have infinitely many closed points
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $Z\subseteq X$ is an irreducible closed subset [def-weil-irreducible-components] with positive topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], then $Z$ contains infinitely many closed points of $X$ [def-weil-closed-points].

source.place: Tags 0478 and 0A21, together with the affine positive-dimension argument in Commutative Algebra (a positive-dimensional finitely generated domain has infinitely many maximal ideals)

proof.text: Give $Z$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; composing the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ is locally of finite type over $k$, and it is irreducible. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ meeting $Z$, and put $V=U\cap Z$. By part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], the open subscheme $V$ of $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A=R/I$, where $I$ is the radical ideal with $V(I)=V$; $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and since $V$ is irreducible the radical ideal $I$ is prime, so $A$ is a domain. Applying [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] to $Z_{\mathrm{red}}$ shows that $V$ has positive dimension, so $A$ has positive Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. The closed points of $V$ correspond to maximal ideals of $A$, whose inverse images in $R$ are maximal ideals.

source.place: Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), part (3), reduction to a nonempty affine open of the irreducible locally algebraic closed subset

proof.text: By [lem-sc-fg-domain-positive-dimension-infinite-maximals], the positive-dimensional finitely generated domain $A$ has infinitely many maximal ideals. These give infinitely many closed points of $V$, and their inverse images are closed points of the affine open $U$.

source.place: the affine positive-dimension argument following Algebra Lemma 00G1

proof.text: Each inverse-image point is a closed point of $U$, so it is a closed point of $X$ by [lem-sc-affine-maximal-points-closed-in-lft-scheme]. Since the points lie in $V\subseteq Z$, they are infinitely many closed points of $X$ contained in $Z$.
